pr_title: tests: threads: fix uninitialized scalar variable
pr_body:
In the file variable val is not initialized,
causing the variable stack_ptr, pos, points to uninitialized data.
Initialize the variable val according to the code and commits.

Fixes #37916

Signed-off-by: Naiyuan Tian <naiyuan.tian@intel.com>
pr_comments: @naiyuantian You need to add into message body, not into title "Fixes #Github_Issue_Number". Use a Github issue number, not a Coverity issue number.
@naiyuantian I think Coverity wants you to initialize `val` in its declaration like `uint8_t val=0;`

issue_context.title: [Coverity CID :219656] Uninitialized scalar variable in file /tests/kernel/threads/thread_stack/src/main.c
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Category: Uninitialized scalar variable
Function: stack_buffer_scenarios
Component: Tests
CID: 219656

Static code scan issues found in file:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/tree/main/tests/kernel/threads/thread_stack/src/main.c

1. In function `void stack_buffer_scenarios(void)` declaring variable `val` without initializer in L95.
2. Then in L164 assigning `stack_ptr = &val`, which points to uninitialized data.
3. In for loop in L165 assigning `pos = stack_ptr`, which points to uninitialized data.
4. Then in L167 `val = *pos;` Coverity raised next violation that uninitialized scalar variable (UNINIT), using uninitialized value `*pos`.


Please fix or provide comments in coverity using the link:
[scan9.coverity.com/reports.htm#v32951/p12996](https://scan9.coverity.com/reports.htm#v32951/p12996)

Note: This issue was created manually.

review_comments: As I said in the comment, Coverity wants you to initialize val in its declaration like uint8_t val=0;
